newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIA'S TRADE BALANCE DEFICIT SHRINKS 3.3 PCT.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIA'S TRADE BALANCE DEFICIT SHRINKS 3.3 PCT.

text.p: Colombia's balance of trade deficit shrank 3.3 percent in the five months January to May, according to figures published Wednesday by the National Statistics Department (DANE).
In that period exports rose 8.1 percent while imports grew 5.8 percent compared with the same period in the previous year, the DANE statement said.
In dollar terms the deficit shrank to $877.3 million free-on- board (FOB) in the first five months of this year compared with $906.8 million in the same period of 1996.
The value of Colombia's exports rose to $4.6 billion FOB between January and May compared with $4.2 billion FOB in the same period in 1996.

So-called traditional exports rose 14.8 percent in value and 11.6 percent in volume. Coffee exports rose 42.6 percent, coal exports were up 18 percent and foreign sales of crude and derivatives gained a wafer-thin 0.2 percent.

Non-traditional exports, excluding gold and emeralds, rose 6.4 percent, DANE said. The biggest rise was in the exports of vehicles and spare parts, up 39.4 percent, while chemical products gained 36.3 percent compared with the same period the previous year.
The value of imports into Colombia between January and May grew to $5.8 billion CIF (cost, insurance and freight) from $5.5 billion CIF a year ago.
The main increase came in supplies and materials for industry.
